newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria suggests divesting from oil production.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria suggests divesting from oil production.

text.p: Nigerian finance minister Anthony Ani on Wednesday said government participation in oil production needed to be reviewed and eventually eliminated.

"Government should gradually divest itself of the 57 percent equity of oil rights so that at the end of the day oil companies and the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation should invest their funds in the exploration of oil," Ani told an economic conference in the Nigerian capital.
"Government should be contented with the receipt of appropriate rents, royalties and petroleum profit tax."
Nigeria currently owns 57 percent of oil rights, and contributes an equivalent amount to joint ventures run in conjunction with foreign partners.
The joint venture partners manage production and exploration.

In the past this has led to acrimony between the two sides - - with oil companies complaining that government has not met cash call obligations, and the government saying the oil companies demand too much money. Nigeria pumps around two million barrels of crude oil a day.
The five biggest joint venture partners are Shell, Chevron, Elf, Mobil and Agip.
